details.expected: Driving begins with a choice: whether this person, this vehicle and this journey are ready to go together. Sweden’s Vision Zero (Nollvisionen) aims for no one to be killed or seriously injured in traffic. The choices taught here contribute to that aim. Trafikverket: Vision Zero Learning rules matters, but so does recognising when a different plan is safer. This module helps you build both habits.

details.expected: Requirements. For an ordinary new category B licence, you need a valid learner permit, permanent residence in Sweden or at least six months of study here, the minimum age of 18, valid car risk training, and successful theory and practical tests. Holding another EEA licence affects the application route. Category B normally covers a passenger car or light goods vehicle with a registered maximum weight of no more than 3,500 kg; trailers are explained in module 8. Check any conditions on your entitlement, including an automatic-transmission restriction. Transportstyrelsen: category B

details.expected: Private practice requires an approved supervisor for the particular learner. The learner normally needs a group 1 permit. Practice in a passenger car can begin at 16; the minimum is 17 years and 6 months for practice with a light goods vehicle or a light trailer. The supervisor is legally treated as the driver, must carry proof of approval, and the practice sign must be clearly visible from behind. Exceptions concerning an existing entitlement must be checked against your own circumstances. Transportstyrelsen: category B

details.expected: Alcohol can affect judgement, attention, vision, reactions and coordination. Feeling normal does not measure those effects. Performance can remain impaired the next day. Do not use a fixed number of hours, a shower, coffee or a calculation as a personal clearance to drive. Ask your prescriber or pharmacist about medicines and driving; do not change a prescribed treatment simply to make a journey. Trafikverket: effects of alcohol and medicines

Sleep and safe judgement

details.expected: Medical explanation · Sleep and awareness. Microsleep (mikrosömn) is a brief, unintended episode of sleep. You do not choose it or reliably prevent it by deciding to try harder. For a deliberately hypothetical two-second lapse at a constant 90 km/h, distance = speed × time: 90 ÷ 3.6 = 25 metres per second; 25 × 2 = 50 metres travelled while asleep. Two seconds is an example, not a prediction of how long a microsleep lasts. CDC/NIOSH: microsleeps

Two seconds is an example, not a prediction of how long a microsleep lasts. CDC/NIOSH: microsleeps

details.expected: Official safety advice · Replace missing sleep with sleep. Adequate sleep is the fundamental remedy for sleep deprivation. Coffee or an energy drink may briefly make you feel more alert, but does not replace the sleep you need; serious sleep deprivation can still lead to microsleep. Music, an open window or willpower should not be treated as a clearance to drive: they do not provide the missing sleep. Do not start when you cannot stay awake; if sleepiness develops, stop somewhere safe and arrange rest or another way to travel. See M07-L03 for planning around fatigue on a journey. NHTSA: drowsy driving

details.expected: Medical explanation · Stimulation is not safe judgement. Stimulant misuse, for example involving amphetamine or cocaine, can produce overconfidence while judgement and concentration are impaired. Some stimulant effects can reduce the feeling of fatigue or drowsiness: tiredness may be masked rather than the need for sleep removed. Feeling energetic is therefore not proof of safe driving ability. Effects vary with substance, dose and individual circumstances; this does not mean every prescribed stimulant treatment has the same effect. Ask your prescriber about your treatment and driving. Swedish Government: stimulant confidence and judgement · NHTSA: stimulant effects

details.expected: Official policy aim · Vision Zero. Nollvisionen means no one should be killed or seriously injured in traffic. It is not a promise that nobody will ever make a mistake. Trafikverket describes shared responsibility: road users must show consideration and judgement and follow traffic rules, while system designers have ultimate responsibility for the system’s safety. Your part includes choosing safe speed and margins and refusing a pressured manoeuvre; road and vehicle design also contribute. For example, staying behind a vehicle near a hidden crest helps protect people even when a passenger dislikes the delay. Trafikverket: Vision Zero

checks.name: Actual reader visited every top-level block
M01/introduction reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Driving begins with a choice: whether this person, this vehicle and this journey are ready to go together. Sweden’s Vision Zero (Nollvisionen) aims for no one to be killed or seriously injured in traffic. The choices taught here contribute to that aim. Trafikverket: Vision Zero Learning rules matters, but so does recognising when a different plan is safer. This module helps you build both habits.

checks.name: M01/disclaimer reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: This material is a learning aid to help you understand Swedish driving theory. It is not an official source and cannot replace official information from Trafikverket and Transportstyrelsen. Always consult their current guidance and the applicable rules.

checks.name: M01/source-dates reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Original sources checked 4 October 2026; G1 additions checked 12 October 2026. Consult current official guidance and applicable rules.

checks.name: M01-L01/goal reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Your goal: Build a personal preparation checklist covering entitlement, permits, supervised practice, risk training and examinations.

checks.name: M01-L01/requirements reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Requirements. For an ordinary new category B licence, you need a valid learner permit, permanent residence in Sweden or at least six months of study here, the minimum age of 18, valid car risk training, and successful theory and practical tests. Holding another EEA licence affects the application route. Category B normally covers a passenger car or light goods vehicle with a registered maximum weight of no more than 3,500 kg; trailers are explained in module 8. Check any conditions on your entitlement, including an automatic-transmission restriction. Transportstyrelsen: category B

checks.name: M01-L01/private-practice reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Private practice requires an approved supervisor for the particular learner. The learner normally needs a group 1 permit. Practice in a passenger car can begin at 16; the minimum is 17 years and 6 months for practice with a light goods vehicle or a light trailer. The supervisor is legally treated as the driver, must carry proof of approval, and the practice sign must be clearly visible from behind. Exceptions concerning an existing entitlement must be checked against your own circumstances. Transportstyrelsen: category B

checks.name: M01-L01/current-changes reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Current changes, checked 1 October 2026. The introductory-course requirement for private practice ended on 1 August 2026. Supervisor approval still applies. This change does not remove mandatory risk training. A theory test passed on or after 19 August 2026 is valid for one year. Tests passed before that date retain the earlier rules; Trafikverket describes the ordinary earlier validity as four months. Check your own result and any approved extension rather than adding a year yourself. Supervisor requirements · Risk training · Test validity amendment · Trafikverket: B tests

checks.name: M01-L01/application-heading reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Apply the learning

checks.name: M01-L01/risk-training reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Risk training has two parts: the first covers alcohol, drugs, fatigue and other risky behaviour; the second covers speed, safety and differing road/weather conditions, including slippery-road training. It must be completed before the tests and remains valid until the licence is obtained or for at most five years. Car and motorcycle risk training are not interchangeable. Transportstyrelsen: risk training

checks.name: M01-L01/checklist reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Build your checklist. Record your permit, supervisor approval if practising privately, entitlement conditions, risk-training status, test preparation and any support application. Use actual expiry dates from your records. Schedule practice around skills you need to improve, not only around an available test slot.

checks.name: M01-L01/worked-decision reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Worked decision. Noor plans to practise privately in September 2026. Her relative says no approvals are needed because a course was abolished. Noor checks the current supervisor page and waits for supervisor approval. The removed course and the retained approval are different requirements.

checks.name: M01-L01/knowledge-check reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Knowledge check. Does a theory pass from July 2026 automatically become valid for a year?

checks.name: M01-L01/remember reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Remember: Plan the administrative route and the learning route together.

checks.name: M01-L02/goal reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Your goal: Decide whether to drive when tiredness, illness, medication, alcohol or drugs may affect you, and explain a safer alternative.

checks.name: M01-L02/fitness-requirement reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Requirement. You must not drive when illness, exhaustion, alcohol, other substances or another condition prevents safe control. A legal alcohol threshold is not a guarantee that you are capable of driving safely. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

checks.name: M01-L02/alcohol-limits reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Trafikverket states that the blood-alcohol limit for drink-driving is 0.2 per mille. For an aggravated offence, factors include at least 1.0 per mille, substantial impairment, or driving that creates a clear traffic danger. Non-prescribed narcotics are subject to a zero-tolerance rule. Properly prescribed medication does not make impaired driving acceptable. Trafikverket: drink-driving law · Alcohol, drugs and medication

checks.name: M01-L02/impairment reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Alcohol can affect judgement, attention, vision, reactions and coordination. Feeling normal does not measure those effects. Performance can remain impaired the next day. Do not use a fixed number of hours, a shower, coffee or a calculation as a personal clearance to drive. Ask your prescriber or pharmacist about medicines and driving; do not change a prescribed treatment simply to make a journey. Trafikverket: effects of alcohol and medicines

checks.name: M01-L02/readiness reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Learning approach. Before taking the keys, ask: Can I stay alert? Can I see and move well enough? Has anything changed since I last drove? Can I concentrate on several developing situations? If the answers are uncertain, make a different travel plan and resolve the uncertainty first. Medical eligibility and day-to-day readiness are related but different: having a licence does not mean you are fit for every journey. Medical requirements

checks.name: M01-L02/sleep-heading reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Sleep and safe judgement

checks.name: M01-L02/microsleep reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Medical explanation · Sleep and awareness. Microsleep (mikrosömn) is a brief, unintended episode of sleep. You do not choose it or reliably prevent it by deciding to try harder. For a deliberately hypothetical two-second lapse at a constant 90 km/h, distance = speed × time: 90 ÷ 3.6 = 25 metres per second; 25 × 2 = 50 metres travelled while asleep. Two seconds is an example, not a prediction of how long a microsleep lasts. CDC/NIOSH: microsleeps

checks.name: M01-L02/sleep-advice reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Official safety advice · Replace missing sleep with sleep. Adequate sleep is the fundamental remedy for sleep deprivation. Coffee or an energy drink may briefly make you feel more alert, but does not replace the sleep you need; serious sleep deprivation can still lead to microsleep. Music, an open window or willpower should not be treated as a clearance to drive: they do not provide the missing sleep. Do not start when you cannot stay awake; if sleepiness develops, stop somewhere safe and arrange rest or another way to travel. See M07-L03 for planning around fatigue on a journey. NHTSA: drowsy driving

checks.name: M01-L02/stimulants reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Medical explanation · Stimulation is not safe judgement. Stimulant misuse, for example involving amphetamine or cocaine, can produce overconfidence while judgement and concentration are impaired. Some stimulant effects can reduce the feeling of fatigue or drowsiness: tiredness may be masked rather than the need for sleep removed. Feeling energetic is therefore not proof of safe driving ability. Effects vary with substance, dose and individual circumstances; this does not mean every prescribed stimulant treatment has the same effect. Ask your prescriber about your treatment and driving. Swedish Government: stimulant confidence and judgement · NHTSA: stimulant effects

checks.name: M01-L02/practice-example reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Practice example. Lina slept too little before an evening journey. She suggests an energy drink and loud music; her friend suggests a stimulant to make her feel confident. The missing sleep remains unresolved, and a stronger feeling of alertness cannot certify safe judgement. She postpones the drive or arranges an alert driver, and makes time for adequate sleep before driving again.

expected_segments: Apply the learning

expected_segments: A tired learner and a companion pause beside a parked car. The keys remain on the bench.

checks.name: M01-L02/worked-decision reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Worked decision. A driver has taken a new medicine and feels unusually drowsy. A passenger offers to keep talking to help them stay awake. The safer choice is to arrange another driver or transport and ask for medication advice. Conversation does not resolve the impairment.

checks.name: M01-L02/knowledge-check reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Knowledge check. (1) Is driving automatically acceptable if a medicine was prescribed correctly? (2) How does microsleep differ from choosing to close your eyes? (3) A sleep-deprived driver feels energetic and unusually confident after taking a stimulant. Has the missing sleep been remedied, and does that feeling establish safe judgement?

checks.name: M01-L02/remember reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Remember: Decide fitness before deciding convenience.

checks.name: M01-L03/goal reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Your goal: Identify how peers, impulses, confidence and personal circumstances can change a decision, and rehearse a refusal or alternative.

checks.name: M01-L03/syllabus reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: The official education syllabus asks learners to reflect on social influence, impulsive decisions, personal motives and their own limitations. These are skills to practise, not labels to attach to an age group or personality. Category B syllabus, chapter 5

checks.name: M01-L03/motives reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Learning approach. Separate the journey's purpose from the feeling of the moment. “Get everyone home” is a purpose. “Show that I can handle this bend quickly” is a different motive. When a passenger's request changes your speed, following distance or willingness to overtake, name the change before acting on it.

checks.name: M01-L03/boundaries reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: A useful personal boundary is a sentence you can use without debate: “I will stop somewhere safe before changing the route”; “I am not passing here”; or “We need another way home.” These are original rehearsal tools, not official scripts. Practise them before a difficult situation, and agree that passengers will help with navigation only when asked.

checks.name: M01-L03/care-requirement reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Requirement. You still owe care to other road users and must adapt speed to conditions. Cooperation does not authorise ignoring a traffic rule because another person is impatient. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §1 and chapter 3 §14

checks.name: M01-L03/vision-zero reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Official policy aim · Vision Zero. Nollvisionen means no one should be killed or seriously injured in traffic. It is not a promise that nobody will ever make a mistake. Trafikverket describes shared responsibility: road users must show consideration and judgement and follow traffic rules, while system designers have ultimate responsibility for the system’s safety. Your part includes choosing safe speed and margins and refusing a pressured manoeuvre; road and vehicle design also contribute. For example, staying behind a vehicle near a hidden crest helps protect people even when a passenger dislikes the delay. Trafikverket: Vision Zero

checks.name: M01-L03/application-heading reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Apply the learning

checks.name: M01-L03/illustration reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: A passenger talks to the driver. In the road view, the car remains behind a van near a crest. Illustration, not a scale diagram of following distance.

checks.name: M01-L03/worked-decision reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Worked decision. Friends laugh when Amir stays behind a slow vehicle on a road with a hidden crest. He recognises the urge to prove himself, maintains space and waits for a genuinely suitable opportunity. His decision protects the purpose of the trip: arriving safely. There is no need to “win” the interaction.

checks.name: M01-L03/knowledge-check reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Knowledge check. (1) Which is better evidence of readiness: feeling confident, or repeatedly identifying hazards and responding safely during supervised practice? (2) Does Vision Zero aim only to reduce minor collisions, or to prevent deaths and serious injuries?

checks.name: M01-L03/remember reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Remember: A decision can be socially uncomfortable and still be the correct driving decision.

checks.name: M01-L04/goal reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Your goal: Compare route, departure time, travel mode and passenger choices for safety, accessibility and environmental impact.

checks.name: M01-L04/advice-attribution reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Official advice · Trafikverket

checks.name: M01-L04/journey-advice reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Trafikverket recommends checking forecasts and traffic conditions, allowing time, taking breaks on longer trips and preparing supplies appropriate to the season. The education syllabus also asks you to consider whether a car is the right means of transport and how passengers or timing affect a journey. Journey advice · Syllabus, chapters 4–5

checks.name: M01-L04/planning reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Learning approach. Plan a usable journey rather than an ideal arrival time. Check where you can rest, refuel or charge as appropriate to the vehicle, and stop legally at the destination. Arrange restraints and space for passengers before departure. If the route has unfamiliar junctions or restrictions, identify them while parked.

checks.name: M01-L04/alternatives reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Compare realistic alternatives. Walking, cycling or public transport may suit some journeys; a car may be necessary for others. Consider access needs, luggage, the return trip and the conditions at the time you will actually travel. A plan that depends on rushing after a late appointment is already fragile.

expected_segments: Apply the learning

checks.name: M01-L04/illustration reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Viewed over their shoulders, two people study a digital map on a tablet facing them. Rain falls outside. The map is illustrative, not live route guidance.

checks.name: M01-L04/worked-decision reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Worked decision. A learner and supervisor can practise on a familiar route in daylight or travel through an unfamiliar town during a forecast snow shower. They choose daylight practice today and plan a later lesson for more demanding conditions with suitable preparation. This is staged learning, not an assumption that difficult conditions can always be avoided.
